ai.title: Upgrade agent models to Opus 4.7
ai.summary: Agent definitions and CLI configurations now default to anthropic/claude-opus-4.7, replacing anthropic/claude-opus-4.6. The ModelName type in agents/types/agent-definition.ts adds 4.7 and 4.5, retaining 4.6 for backward compatibility. Updated files include .agents/*-cli.ts, agents/editor/*, agents/thinker/*, and agents/reviewer/*.

eli5.text: The assistant now uses a newer model version across all its default settings, so tasks run through the agent system will use the updated model instead of the previous one. If you interact with an integrated agent (such as the editor or thinker agents), you are affected. You would not notice anything visual, but the underlying model name changed in the configuration.

ai.title: Fix Anthropic double-charge bug in OpenRouter cost extraction
ai.summary: Cost extraction now uses `Math.max` instead of summing `usage.cost` and `usage.cost_details.upstream_inference_cost` in `web/src/llm-api/openrouter.ts`. OpenRouter reports identical billed values in both fields for Anthropic routes, causing double-charging when summed. The fix applies strict type checks to safely handle null or missing cost details across different provider shapes.

eli5.text: The system that tracks how much you've been charged for using Claude through OpenRouter stopped accidentally charging you twice for the same thing. OpenRouter was telling the system the same cost in two separate fields, and the system added them together, effectively doubling your bill on every Anthropic request. Now it picks the higher of the two reported numbers instead, which correctly reflects what you were actually charged, and it handles the case where one of the fields is missing entirely. This fix is live in production.

ai.title: query-message-costs.ts script for BigQuery cost investigation
ai.summary: Added scripts/query-message-costs.ts to query BigQuery `message` table for cost and upstream_inference_cost fields. Investigates potential double-counting in web/src/llm-api/openrouter.ts#extractUsageAndCost when OpenRouter populates both fields for non-BYOK requests. Supports --prod, --limit, and --model flags for targeted analysis.

eli5.text: The team added a new internal tool that lets them dig through their billing records to check whether OpenRouter is accidentally charging people twice for the same request. When you send a message through OpenRouter, the cost gets recorded twice in the system; once as a general charge and once as an 'upstream' charge, so the tool looks at recent messages to see if that's happening for regular (non-BYOK) requests. If you ran this tool today, you'd see a table of messages with columns showing cost, upstream charge, and how they should compare. The fix to stop double-charging is recorded in a separate change in this snapshot, but this investigation script is now in place to help verify whether it's working.

ai.title: Fix free-tier credit overdraw and debt accounting
ai.summary: Added `shouldBlockFreeUserOverdraw` gate and `InsufficientCreditsError` to prevent free-tier users from overdrawing credits. `consumeFromOrderedGrants` no longer repays debt; it only deepens it on overflow, with debt cleared exclusively in `grant-credits.ts` when new credits are added. Changes apply to `packages/billing/src/balance-calculator.ts` and `packages/billing/src/grant-credits.ts`. The debt model now strictly separates consumption (deepening) from granting (clearing).

eli5.text: Free-tier users (those who have never purchased credits or a subscription) can now be blocked from using more credits than they actually have, preventing people from farming free credits and spending far more than intended. When a free-tier user tries to make a charge that would drop their balance below zero, the system will now stop the charge instead of letting it go through. Paid users with subscriptions or purchases are unaffected: they can still build up a negative balance, but only new credit grants will clear that debt, not regular usage. This is live today as a hard gate in the billing system.

ai.title: Refine skill loading prompt in base2 agent
ai.summary: The base2 agent's implementation step prompt was updated to change how it instructs skill loading. The directive shifted from a mandatory 'must use' command to a conditional 'consider loading' suggestion. It now explicitly warns against reloading skills already present in the conversation context. This change is isolated to `agents/base2/base2.ts`.

eli5.text: The agent now gently suggests loading skills instead of making it a strict requirement. When you work with the assistant, it will look at what skills it needs, load them, and remember not to load the same ones again during your chat. You won't notice the change unless you're paying close attention to how the assistant handles its tools.

ai.title: Remove initial free credit grant on signup
ai.summary: Removed createInitialCreditGrant and processAndGrantCredit calls from NextAuth sign-in callbacks in freebuff/web/src/app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/auth-options.ts and web/src/app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/auth-options.ts. New accounts no longer receive DEFAULT_FREE_CREDITS_GRANT. Stripe customer linking remains, but credit initialization logic is deleted. Existing users retain current balances.

eli5.text: When someone signs up for a new account, they will no longer automatically receive free credits added to their balance. The signup process now skips the step that used to grant a set number of credits to new users, so brand-new accounts start at zero. People who already have accounts keep whatever credits they had before.

ai.title: Referral credits disabled via zero bonus constant
ai.summary: Referral credit grants disabled by setting CREDITS_REFERRAL_BONUS to 0 in common/src/constants/limits.ts. web/src/app/api/referrals/helpers.ts skips ledger writes when bonus is zero, preserving referral tracking records only. Mechanism targets self-referral abuse patterns while shifting focus to Freebuff's non-credit model.

eli5.text: When someone signs up using a friend's referral link on Freebuff, neither person will anymore receive 500 free credits as a thank-you for bringing in new users. Referrals made through shared links will still be recorded so the platform can see who referred whom, but the actual credit rewards that used to be granted automatically have been turned off. This appears to be a response to cases where people created multiple accounts just to earn and then burn large amounts of free credits, and the company is now shifting away from relying on credits altogether in favor of Freebuff's credit-free model.

ai.title: Block codebuff usage
ai.summary: Added `created_at` to `User` type and `userColumns` in `common/src/types/contracts/database.ts`, and `principals` to `GetUserUsageDataFn` in `common/src/types/contracts/billing.ts`. `web/src/app/api/v1/chat/completions/_post.ts` now rejects non-free mode requests if the account is under 3 days old or lacks a paid relationship (purchase/subscription > 0), unless BYOK is used. `web/src/app/api/v1/me/_get.ts` updated to handle `Date` types in the response record.

eli5.text: If you sign up for a new account today and immediately try to use advanced AI features that cost money, the service will now stop you unless you have a paid subscription or purchase history. Accounts must be at least three days old and linked to a real payment method to use anything beyond the free tier. People who provide their own AI service key (BYOK) skip this check entirely, since they're paying their own bill directly.

ai.title: Fix completions test type errors
ai.summary: Added explicit Record<string, number> type assertions to breakdown and principals fields in completions.test.ts. Resolved TypeScript compilation errors during test execution. Internal change affecting only web/src/app/api/v1/chat/completions/__tests__/completions.test.ts.

eli5.text: The automated checks that make sure the chat completion endpoint behaves correctly were crashing because two fields in the test data didn't match the expected shape. The developers corrected the test fixture so the fake billing object now declares its 'breakdown' and 'principals' maps as explicitly empty dictionaries, letting the suite compile and run. This is internal reliability work: nothing changes for you, but the team can trust their tests again.

ai.title: Fix types in e2e-mocks and SDK tests
ai.summary: Added missing created_at field to MOCK_USER in sdk/e2e/utils/e2e-mocks.ts. Type errors in SDK test suites (run-cancellation, run-file-filter, run-handle-event, run-mcp-tool-filter) resolved. Internal type alignment for e2e utilities and unit tests.

eli5.text: If you are a developer using this system to build apps, your code checks (a kind of testing tool) now run without errors related to a missing field on the fake user data used during testing. The testing utilities that simulate a user now include the account creation date field, which was previously missing and causing type errors. This only affects your local development and testing work, not anything your end users see.

ai.title: Add createdat to agent runtime test fixtures
ai.summary: Added `created_at: new Date('2024-01-01T00:00:00Z')` to mock user objects in `common/src/testing/fixtures/agent-runtime.ts` and `evals/impl/agent-runtime.ts`. This fixes type errors where the `created_at` field was missing from the test fixtures but required by the runtime schema. Scope covers shared core testing fixtures and the evals implementation. The field uses a fixed ISO 8601 timestamp to ensure deterministic test results.

eli5.text: The test versions of the system's example user accounts now include a fake signup date of January 1, 2024. You wouldn't notice this yourself since it only affects internal testing files, not the live application. The testing tool flagged that these sample users were missing a date field that the system expects, so adding it stops the tests from producing confusing errors about missing information.

ai.title: Generation-lookup fallback bills OpenRouter streams missing usage
ai.summary: Added `ensureBilled` and `fallbackBillFromGeneration` to `web/src/llm-api/openrouter.ts` to capture `generationId` and `model` from stream chunks. If a stream exits without a usage-bearing chunk, a 500ms delay triggers a lookup of OpenRouter's `/generation` endpoint to bill the final cost. This prevents free completion tokens when mid-stream failures occur.

eli5.text: If an AI response you're getting cut off early, say, the connection drops or the AI hiccups mid-response, the system used to potentially skip charging you for the tokens already generated. Now, it captures the generation ID from the first response chunk and, after stream ends, waits 500ms before looking up the final cost from OpenRouter's records to ensure billing is still recorded. Developers reviewing the code would notice the StreamState type now tracks generationId, model, and billed status, with fallbackBillFromGeneration handling the delayed cost lookup.

ai.title: Chat completions endpoint allow freemode requests
ai.summary: Chat completions API now permits freemode requests, bypassing paid relationship and account age validation. Root cause: `isFreeModeRequest` flag added to conditional check in `_post.ts`. Scope: `web/src/app/api/v1/chat/completions/_post.ts`.

eli5.text: The chat completions endpoint now accepts requests from free mode users, bypassing paid relationship and account age validation. Free mode users can now make requests to the chat completions API without needing a paid account or meeting the minimum account age requirement. If you looked at the code, you'd see a new conditional check that skips the paid relationship and account age validation when the request comes from free mode.

ai.title: Add Fireworks cache interval test script
ai.summary: New `scripts/test-fireworks-cache-intervals.ts` measures Fireworks prompt caching persistence across idle intervals. Sends priming request, waits configurable intervals, reports cache hit rates. Supports `glm-5.1`, `kimi-k2.5`, `minimax` models with `--deployment` and `--intervals` flags. Internal tooling only.

eli5.text: Your team added an internal test tool that checks how long the AI provider keeps your saved prompt in fast memory before it gets thrown away. It sends one prompt, waits different amounts of time (like 30 seconds, 5 minutes, up to about 35 minutes), then sends the same prompt again to see if the provider remembers it and gives a discount. This only runs on your internal machines and doesn't change anything you see right now, but it will help figure out how long you can pause between questions before you have to wait for the full prompt to load again.

ai.title: Fireworks health monitor added
ai.summary: New server-side monitor scrapes Fireworks Prometheus metrics every 60s, computes per-deployment health snapshots, and exposes /api/admin/fireworks-health. Static config moved to fireworks-config.ts to avoid edge-runtime import issues. CLI script scripts/check-fireworks-health.ts added for ad-hoc verification. Monitor auto-starts via instrumentation.ts register().

eli5.text: A new behind-the-scenes watchdog is now running: it wakes up every minute, checks on the health of several AI model services, and quietly records whether each one is working normally, slowing down, or having errors. The engineering team can look up that health report whenever they want, and there's also a quick command they can run to double-check things on the spot. One thing that was moved around is now stored in a safer spot, which stops certain setup steps from crashing when the system starts up.

ai.title: Decouple billing from message insert
ai.summary: Isolated credit consumption from message insertion in `packages/billing/src/balance-calculator.ts` to ensure audit rows record upstream OpenRouter costs even if billing fails. Removed `shouldBlockFreeUserOverdraw` and `InsufficientCreditsError`, replacing the hard gate with idempotency checks on `messageId` to prevent duplicate charges on retries. Scope covers `packages/billing/src/balance-calculator.ts` and associated tests. Billing errors now log loudly but allow message insertion with `credits=0` to preserve cost visibility.

eli5.text: If the system that charges you for using the assistant hiccups, your message will still get saved and you won't lose access to use the assistant. Previously, a billing failure could block your message from being recorded and potentially cut off your usage, but now billing is separated from message insertion and retries won't double-charge you. You'd notice this as continued service availability even when billing issues occur, with zero-impact retries preserving your session.

ai.title: Add paid-gate bypass for team@codebuff.com
ai.summary: Added `PAID_GATE_BYPASS_EMAILS` set containing `team@codebuff.com` to bypass the paid+aged-account gate in `web/src/app/api/v1/chat/completions/_post.ts`. This allows integration tests, such as the SDK prompt-caching test, to run against a real server without seeding a purchase for every fresh test account. The bypass checks `userInfo.email` (case-insensitive) before evaluating `hasPaidRelationship` and `accountIsTooNew`.

eli5.text: If you send a chat-api request using the email team@codebuff.com, the system lets your request through even before you have paid or waited three days for your account to mature, so the company's own integration tests can hit a real server without buying a subscription for every fresh test account. Today, any request not coming from that address still has to clear the pay-and-wait gate; the bypass only applies to that single email address.

ai.title: Free mode rejects non-allowlisted agent model
ai.summary: Added validation in web/src/app/api/v1/chat/completions/_post.ts to reject free-mode requests using non-allowlisted agent+model combinations via isFreeModeAllowedAgentModel. Prevents unpaid accounts from bypassing cost checks to request expensive models (e.g. Opus) on the OpenRouter key. Returns 403 with error 'free_mode_invalid_agent_model' and logs analytics event CHAT_COMPLETIONS_VALIDATION_ERROR. Check runs before rate limiting and OpenRouter calls.

eli5.text: Free accounts can no longer request expensive models like Opus while pretending to use free mode, which previously let them bypass billing checks and get costly responses at no charge. Going forward, an unpaid account that tries to set the request to 'free' must also pick an agent and model that are on the short allowlist; anything else is rejected with a 403 error before the request reaches the rate limiter or the model provider, and the failed attempt is recorded for review. This restriction is live today and applies to any free-tier account attempting to exploit the loophole.
